findings.finding: PMP entry count correctly detected at runtime by probing PMPADDR CSRs (0-63) via __check_csr_64 macro. Each CSR is write-then-read-back verified; pmp_count incremented only for CSRs holding the written all-ones pattern. Matches spec norm:pmp_entry_count (machine.adoc:3347-3349) for 0/16/64 entry implementations.

spec_citations.excerpt: Up to 64 PMP entries are supported. Implementations may implement zero, 16, or 64 PMP entries; the lowest-numbered PMP entries must be implemented first.
Software may determine the PMP granularity by writing zero to pmp0cfg, then writing all ones to pmpaddr0, then reading back pmpaddr0.

findings.finding: Runtime bounds check uses probed pmp_count (not PMP_COUNT=64) to validate PMP indices before programming. Both configure functions guard all entry accesses with this check, preventing writes to unimplemented entries.

pmp_set() uses compile-time PMP_COUNT (64) as a defensive bounds check. All callers (sbi_hart_smepmp_configure, sbi_hart_oldpmp_configure) pre-validate indices via is_valid_pmp_idx() against the runtime pmp_count before calling, so the PMP_COUNT check is a safety net only. PMP entry is programmed in correct order: pmpaddr written first, then pmpcfg — avoids transient NAPOT mis-match.

Two-pass Smepmp configuration: (1) sets RLB to bypass locked-entry enforcement, programs M-only firmware regions; (2) sets MML to enable Smepmp encoding, programs shared/SU-only regions, disables remainder. Issues sfence.vma fence after all PMP writes (line 216) per privileged spec section 3.7.2. Firmware entries tracked in bitmap to survive domain switches.

spec_citations.excerpt: this extension introduces the RLB, MMWP, and MML fields in the mseccfg CSR and their associated rules.

findings.finding: Traditional (non-Smepmp) PMP configuration correctly iterates over domain memory regions, translates flags via sbi_domain_get_oldpmp_flags(), programs entries within runtime pmp_count bounds, disables remaining entries, and issues fence.

Boston platform hardcodes PMP writes to entries 14-15 (PMPADDR14, PMPADDR15, PMPCFG2) before runtime PMP count detection runs. No read-back verification to confirm writes took effect. If hardware implements fewer than 16 entries (e.g., 0), these writes are silently ignored due to WARL behavior, leaving DRAM unprotected. Platform-specific code assumes 16 entries; only safe because the MIPS Boston platform is known to implement 16 PMP entries.

findings.finding: ESWIN EIC770X hardcodes PMP slot layout constants assuming exactly 8 PMP entries (PMP_FW_START=0, PMP_RESERVED_B=6, PMP_FREE_B_START=7). No runtime verification that pmp_count >= PMP_FREE_B_START + PMP_FREE_B_COUNT (i.e., >= 8). If a variant implements fewer PMP entries, the hardcoded indices could access unimplemented CSRs (WARL ignored) or skip programming entirely.
findings.snippet:
#define PMP_FW_START 0
#define PMP_FW_COUNT 2
#define PMP_RESERVED_A 2
#define PMP_FREE_A_START 3
#define PMP_FREE_A_COUNT 3
#define PMP_RESERVED_B 6
#define PMP_FREE_B_START 7
#define PMP_FREE_B_COUNT 1

findings.finding: Stack arrays sized to PMP_COUNT (64), the architectural maximum. Actual iteration bound comes from domain memregion count (sbi_domain_for_each_memregion), not from PMP_COUNT. Over-allocation uses ~512 bytes of stack but has no security impact.
